1.explanation:
1. We require Prettier’s API (`require('prettier')`).
2. We provide the sample Markdown table exactly as in the bug report (with long HTML cell contents).
3. We call `prettier.format(input, options)` with `parser: 'markdown'`, default `printWidth: 80`, and `proseWrap: 'preserve'` to disable wrapping of the HTML.
4. When you run this script (`node reproduce-long-table-separator.js`), you will see that the generated separator line between header and body is padded to match the longest cell (resulting in a ~865-character long line), reproducing the bug.
1.bug_scenario: When formatting a GitHub-style “all-contributors” Markdown table containing large chunks of HTML in its cells, Prettier’s table printer still measures the longest cell width (which can be hundreds of characters) and produces a separator row padded to that width. In our example the header separator line becomes over 865 characters long, exceeding any reasonable print width and defeating the purpose of human-readable tables.
